principle.name: Battery Efficiency First
principle.description: Always prioritize battery life and performance optimization in mobile development. Mobile apps run on resource-constrained devices with limited battery capacity, making efficiency crucial for user experience.
principle.rationale: Users abandon apps that drain battery quickly. Efficient apps retain users longer and receive better ratings.

example.good: Use efficient scheduling, batch operations, and minimize wake locks
example.bad: Frequent polling, unnecessary location updates, and continuous background processing

principle.name: Platform-Native Experience
principle.description: Follow platform-specific UI/UX guidelines and use native components when appropriate. Each platform has established patterns that users expect.
principle.rationale: Native-feeling apps are more intuitive and receive higher user satisfaction. Platform consistency reduces learning curve.

example.good: iOS uses UINavigationController, Android uses Navigation Component
example.bad: Custom navigation that doesn't match platform expectations

principle.name: Offline-First Architecture
principle.description: Design for offline functionality from the start. Mobile networks are unreliable, and users expect apps to work without connectivity.
principle.rationale: Offline-capable apps provide better user experience in poor network conditions and reduce frustration.

example.good: Local database with sync queue, conflict resolution, and delta sync
example.bad: Online-only operations that fail without network

principle.name: Cross-Platform Code Reuse
principle.description: Maximize shared code between platforms while respecting platform differences. Shared code reduces maintenance burden and ensures consistency.
principle.rationale: Less duplicated code means fewer bugs and faster feature delivery across platforms.

example.good: Shared services, platform-agnostic utilities, and conditional platform rendering

principle.name: Performance Budgeting
principle.description: Establish and monitor performance budgets for key metrics. Mobile devices have varying capabilities, so performance must be actively managed.
principle.rationale: Performance budgets prevent regressions and ensure consistent experience across target devices.

example.good: Cold start under 2 seconds, progressive loading, and optimized bundles
example.bad: Unmonitored startup times that degrade over time

convention.rule: Use platform-agnostic naming with platform-specific prefixes when needed
Organize by platform and shared concerns
convention.template: src/ ├── shared/ # Platform-agnostic code │ ├── services/ │ ├── utils/ │ └── components/ ├── ios/ # iOS-specific code │ ├── native-modules/ │ └── ui/ ├── android/ # Android-specific code │ ├── native-modules/ │ └── ui/ └── platform/ # Platform-specific adapters

pitfall.why_problematic: Creates inconsistent user experience and requires platform-specific workarounds
pitfall.correct_approach: Use platform detection and conditional rendering for platform-specific features

pitfall.why_problematic: Mobile apps have limited memory and processing power; inefficient state management causes crashes and battery drain
pitfall.correct_approach: Use efficient state libraries, minimize re-renders, and implement proper state persistence

pitfall.why_problematic: Background processes that continue when app is not in foreground cause battery drain and may be killed by OS
pitfall.correct_approach: Properly manage app lifecycle, pause background tasks when appropriate, and use efficient scheduling

pitfall.why_problematic: Mobile networks are unreliable; online-only apps fail in poor connectivity conditions
pitfall.correct_approach: Implement offline-first architecture with robust sync mechanisms and conflict resolution

pitfall.why_problematic: Mobile devices have limited RAM; memory leaks cause crashes and poor performance
pitfall.correct_approach: Profile memory usage, implement proper cleanup, use efficient data structures, and avoid memory leaks

category.name: before_starting
category.item: Define target platforms and minimum OS versions
Establish performance budgets (startup time, memory, battery)

category.name: during_implementation
category.item: Follow platform UI/UX guidelines (iOS HIG, Material Design)
Optimize images and assets for mobile
Add comprehensive error handling and recovery
Profile performance and memory usage regularly

category.name: before_completion
category.item: Test on real devices, not just simulators
Ensure app size under 50MB initial download
Test push notifications on both platforms
